Critical Disks

This section describes the geometric bounds used to control the location of critical points and critical values of a polynomial cover.

These bounds are used to construct safe regions in the complex plane for numerical path lifting.

Mathematical background

This section contains a description of the mathematical results used to construsct disks containing all the critical points and all the critical values.

Critical Disks

Many algorithms in PolynomialCovers require constructing paths in the complex plane that avoid the critical values of a polynomial map. To guarantee numerical stability, the package uses explicit bounds to enclose the critical points and critical values in disks centered at the origin.

This section explains the mathematical bounds used to construct those regions.

Polynomial Covers

A polynomial cover is a map

\[P : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}\]

given by

\[P(z) = a_0 z^n + a_1 z^{n-1} + \cdots + a_n ,\]

with (a_0 \neq 0).

The critical points of the map are the solutions of

\[P'(z) = 0 ,\]

and the critical values are their images

\[w_i = P(z_i).\]

The set of critical values plays a central role in the topology of the covering map: path lifting is well-defined precisely on paths that avoid this set.

Cauchy Bound

If

\[P(z) = a_0 z^n + a_1 z^{n-1} + \cdots + a_n ,\]

then every root satisfies

\[|z| \le 1 + \max_{1 \le k \le n} \left|\frac{a_k}{a_0}\right|.\]

This gives a disk centered at the origin containing all roots.

The same bound can be applied to the derivative (P’(z)) to enclose all critical points.

Fujiwara Bound

A sharper estimate is the Fujiwara bound

\[|z| \le 2 \max_{1 \le k \le n} \left|\frac{a_k}{a_0}\right|^{1/k}.\]

This bound is often tighter and therefore produces smaller enclosing disks.

Disk Containing Critical Points

Applying the above bounds to the derivative polynomial

\[P'(z)\]

provides an explicit radius

\[BF(P')\]

such that all critical points satisfy

\[|z| \le BF(P').\]

This defines a disk

\[\mathbb{D}_c = \{ z \in \mathbb{C} : |z| \le BF(P') \}.\]

Disk Containing Critical Values

Once a bound on the critical points is known, we can bound the critical values using the triangle inequality.

If

\[|z| \le R_c ,\]

then

\[|P(z)| \le \sum_{k=0}^{n} |a_k| R_c^{\,n-k}.\]

This produces a radius

\[S_v\]

such that all critical values lie in the disk

\[\mathbb{D}_v = \{ w \in \mathbb{C} : |w| \le R_v \}.\]

Exclusion Radius for Path Lifting

When computing monodromy numerically, paths must remain strictly outside the disk containing critical values.

To ensure this, the disk (D_v) is inflated by a factor (s>1):

\[S = s S_v .\]

We then compute the smallest radius (r) such that

\[|P(z)| > S \quad \text{for all } |z| = r .\]

This guarantees that the circle of radius (r) in the base space lies entirely outside the inflated critical value disk.

Polygonal loops constructed on this circle can therefore be lifted safely without encountering singular fibers.

Role in the Algorithms

These bounds serve several purposes in the algorithms implemented in PolynomialCovers: • providing a safe basepoint outside the critical value region, • constructing loops for monodromy computation, and • guaranteeing numerical stability of path lifting.

Although these bounds are not optimal, they are inexpensive to compute and sufficiently sharp for robust numerical algorithms.
